reasons: Internal control and audit (0 of 4): no material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change or disagreement flagged, so the control environment looks clean.
Prior-period corrections and accounting changes (0 of 3): no restatement/revision, voluntary accounting change or segment change, which removes the strongest historical predictors of misstatement.
Investigations and litigation (0 of 3): no SEC, class action or other government matters flagged.

Financial pressure (0 of 4) and management turnover (0 of 2): no going-concern, covenant, revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay or capital-raise pressure, and no CEO/CFO changes, so motive and opportunity signals are weak.
Numeric warning signals (0 of 4 computable): Beneish M, Dechow F, accruals and cash-flow-to-income tests all fall within normal ranges.

Transaction complexity (1 of 8): a single complexity item (e.g. over-time revenue, customer concentration or an acquisition) is present. This is common and adds only modest judgement risk. Because the card is aggregated, it cannot be identified, so a small premium stays above the base rate.
